## TL;DR

The macOS Hub QA record and XCTest registry isolation fixes are present in the current tree. The recorded QA verifies app build and launch, first-run rendering, local server discovery and connection, and the sign-in page. Signed-in Projects and Tasks remain unverified because human task #1174 has no results.

## Work and rationale

Built the Hub with Xcode, signing disabled, and a task-specific DerivedData directory. Launched through LaunchServices using an isolated support directory. Verified the first-run empty state, discovery and healthy connection to a local RepoOS server, persistence of the server entry, and display of the sign-in page. The QA record documents these observations and uses app-window captures.

The QA run exposed that the XCTest host could write to the developer's normal Hub registry without an explicit support-directory override. The implementation now uses unique temporary storage for XCTest, removes it on host termination, logs cleanup errors, and tests cleanup and failure propagation. The QA record also documents the earlier registry write and its unknown prior selection without claiming restoration.

## Approaches tried

Inspected the native Hub window and accessibility tree while exercising first-run and add-server flows. Tried automated email-code entry, but it did not reach authenticated screens. A direct executable launch did not show a content window during the short observation period; this remains unexplained, not a confirmed crash. Stored report files are managed by RepoOS and were not edited manually.

## Challenges and blockers

A human must sign in through the authorized email-code flow, inspect Projects and Tasks, and record the results in #1174. That human-assigned task remains without results, so authenticated acceptance is open. The full `repoos check` is being run against the current source before handoff. RepoOS will generate round metadata and the change summary after validation.

## Key learnings

Rendering the sign-in page verifies connection and web content only; it does not verify authenticated functionality. The projects and tasks acceptance needs direct observations recorded in the human follow-up. XCTest app-host processes need isolated support storage, with cleanup failures visible. A fresh engineering report draft is required for each handoff because RepoOS consumes it into the immutable round report.
